findings.body: Event creation throws while reading `integration` from undefined instead of falling back to Cal Video, so the booking flow fails.
findings.failure_mode: A valid no-destination event causes a runtime TypeError in EventManager.create.
findings.impact: Event creation throws while reading `integration` from undefined instead of falling back to Cal Video, so the booking flow fails.
findings.root_cause: The newly destructured first array element is treated as always present even though destinationCalendar is optional and may be empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` or explicitly handle the empty-array case before accessing the property.
findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences a missing destination calendar
findings.trigger: A booking selects Google Meet while the event has a null or empty destinationCalendar array, such as a user without a configured destination calendar.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 119 shows `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` accessed without optional chaining after destructuring from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. When the array is empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined, causing TypeError on property access.

findings.body: The database retains only the first destination calendar. Confirmation and payment handlers reconstruct the event from that singular relation, so calendar events are created only for the primary host and secondary hosts never receive their events.
findings.failure_mode: Deferred booking workflows lose secondary-host calendar routing information before calendar creation occurs.
findings.impact: The database retains only the first destination calendar. Confirmation and payment handlers reconstruct the event from that singular relation, so calendar events are created only for the primary host and secondary hosts never receive their events.
findings.root_cause: The new in-memory array is reduced back to index zero when the booking is stored, with no persistence mechanism for the remaining destinations.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist all destination-calendar identities needed by the booking, using an appropriate relation or booking metadata, and reconstruct the complete array in confirmation and payment flows.
findings.title: Only the first collective host calendar is persisted with the booking
findings.trigger: A collective booking has multiple host destination calendars and requires later calendar creation, for example because it requires confirmation or payment.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 1877 shows `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` - only the first destination calendar is persisted to the booking. For collective events with multiple host calendars, secondary calendars are lost.

findings.body: No array entry matches the credential, so the event is created on `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar.
findings.failure_mode: Existing users' bookings are written to the wrong Google calendar.
findings.impact: No array entry matches the credential, so the event is created on `primary` instead of the configured destination calendar.
findings.root_cause: Calendar selection was changed from the configured external ID to an exclusively credential-ID-based lookup without preserving the legacy nullable-credential path.
findings.suggested_fix: When no credential-ID match exists, fall back to the destination selected for the integration or pass the loop's destination external ID directly to GoogleCalendarService.
findings.title: Legacy Google destinations without credential IDs now ignore the selected calendar
findings.trigger: An existing DestinationCalendar has a null `credentialId`, which the schema permits and the old EventManager branch explicitly supports, while its `externalId` points to a non-primary Google calendar.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines 147-149 show credential-based lookup with fallback to 'primary'. When credentialId is null (legacy destinations), find returns undefined and event goes to primary instead of configured calendar.

findings.body: The fallback searches for an external ID equal to null/undefined and always returns undefined, so the Google update request has no calendar ID and fails instead of updating the configured calendar.
findings.failure_mode: Rescheduling or editing legacy Google bookings fails to update their calendar event.
findings.impact: The fallback searches for an external ID equal to null/undefined and always returns undefined, so the Google update request has no calendar ID and fails instead of updating the configured calendar.
findings.root_cause: The fallback branch compares destination IDs against the value already known to be absent.
findings.suggested_fix: When the argument is absent, select the relevant destination calendar directly, preferably by credential ID, with a deliberate `primary` fallback if none exists.
findings.title: Google updates no longer fall back to the event destination calendar
findings.trigger: An older booking reference has a null or missing `externalCalendarId`, while the CalendarEvent contains its configured destination calendar.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 256 shows fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` - when externalCalendarId is falsy, this searches for undefined and always returns undefined.

findings.body: With billing enabled, the organization receives a live slug even though it should remain unpublished under `requestedSlug`; with billing disabled, the slug is omitted and the organization cannot be reached at the requested URL.
findings.failure_mode: Organization publication state is inverted in both billing configurations.
findings.impact: With billing enabled, the organization receives a live slug even though it should remain unpublished under `requestedSlug`; with billing disabled, the slug is omitted and the organization cannot be reached at the requested URL.
findings.root_cause: The refactor changed `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` rather than preserving the original boolean condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the negated condition: include `slug` only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, while keeping `requestedSlug` for the enabled case.
findings.title: Organization slug publication logic is reversed
findings.trigger: An organization is created with either team billing enabled or disabled.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines 151,153 show `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` and `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}`. Original was `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` for slug. Logic is inverted.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- Converts destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent to be an array.
- Patches and fixes so every sentence of code that was using evet.destinationCalendar can support the new type of array.
- The logic here is to fallback to normal behaviour has having one main destinationCalendar but also supports multiple so host can get invited correctly.

Fixes #7754 
## Loom 
Creating event and rescheduling:
https://www.loom.com/share/3cb3af513d274ed2bdfed44e48edddf6?sid=d81ce3de-2893-4a30-b085-ff67c31b7dfb

Canceling event:
https://www.loom.com/share/7ef505d4665e4d4982d2bb2d7b118085?sid=cd43c97c-aa86-4667-979f-f6492adf3365

## Requirement/Documentation

## Type of change

<!-- Please delete bullets that are not relevant. -->

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

- Are there environment variables that should be set? No
- What are the minimal test data to have? Setup a collective event using teampro and teamfree users. Add any app calendar to those accounts and add them as host for collective event.
- What is expected (happy path) to have (input and output)? Collective event with 2 host and every user with any calendar app installed should receive proper calendar events.
- Any other important info that could help to test that PR

## Mandatory Tasks

- [X] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

raw_findings.title: Lark creates every host event in the first host's calendar
raw_findings.trigger: A collective event has two or more Lark hosts and EventManager invokes this service once with each host's credential.

raw_findings.body: The secondary credential requests `/me/calendars/{first-host-calendar-id}/events`; Microsoft Graph cannot resolve or authorize that calendar ID for the secondary mailbox, so its event is not created.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Calendar creation for Office 365 collective hosts fails or targets the wrong mailbox calendar.
raw_findings.impact: The secondary credential requests `/me/calendars/{first-host-calendar-id}/events`; Microsoft Graph cannot resolve or authorize that calendar ID for the secondary mailbox, so its event is not created.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation ignores the per-invocation credential and hard-codes the first destination as the target.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Accept the current credential ID in `createEvent` and choose the matching destination calendar rather than always taking element zero.
raw_findings.title: Office 365 creates every host event in the first host's calendar
raw_findings.trigger: A collective event has multiple Office 365 hosts and the service is instantiated with a secondary host's credential.

raw_findings.body: The secondary account's fetched calendars are filtered using the primary host's external URL, generally yielding no matching calendar and no event for that host.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Secondary CalDAV host events are silently omitted or creation returns an invalid empty result.
raw_findings.impact: The secondary account's fetched calendars are filtered using the primary host's external URL, generally yielding no matching calendar and no event for that host.
raw_findings.root_cause: Multi-account creation still reduces the destination array to its first element.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the current credential identity or destination external ID into this service and filter against the destination corresponding to that invocation.
raw_findings.title: CalDAV creation filters every credential against the first host's calendar URL
raw_findings.trigger: A collective event contains multiple CalDAV-backed hosts and creation runs against a secondary host's account.

raw_findings.body: The subsequent description patch still receives the raw undefined `selectedCalendar`, causing the patch request to fail and leaving the calendar description without the generated meeting link.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The event is created successfully but its follow-up Google Meet metadata update targets an undefined calendar.
raw_findings.impact: The subsequent description patch still receives the raw undefined `selectedCalendar`, causing the patch request to fail and leaving the calendar description without the generated meeting link.
raw_findings.root_cause: The fallback is applied only inline to the insert call rather than to the shared selected-calendar value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute one resolved calendar ID, such as `selectedCalendar ?? "primary"`, and use it for insert and every subsequent patch request.
raw_findings.title: Google Meet patching does not use the new primary-calendar fallback
raw_findings.trigger: A Google event with a generated Hangouts link has no credential-matched destination, so insertion uses the new `primary` fallback.

raw_findings.body: The fallback searches for an external ID equal to null/undefined and always returns undefined, so the Google update request has no calendar ID and fails instead of updating the configured calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Rescheduling or editing legacy Google bookings fails to update their calendar event.
raw_findings.impact: The fallback searches for an external ID equal to null/undefined and always returns undefined, so the Google update request has no calendar ID and fails instead of updating the configured calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: The fallback branch compares destination IDs against the value already known to be absent.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When the argument is absent, select the relevant destination calendar directly, preferably by credential ID, with a deliberate `primary` fallback if none exists.
raw_findings.title: Google updates no longer fall back to the event destination calendar
raw_findings.trigger: An older booking reference has a null or missing `externalCalendarId`, while the CalendarEvent contains its configured destination calendar.

raw_findings.body: The lookup always returns undefined and deletion targets `primary`; the actual event remains in the configured calendar and may continue producing reminders.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cancellation sends a delete request to the wrong Google calendar and leaves the real event orphaned.
raw_findings.impact: The lookup always returns undefined and deletion targets `primary`; the actual event remains in the configured calendar and may continue producing reminders.
raw_findings.root_cause: The absent argument is used as the search key in the fallback branch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the destination by the current credential or use the appropriate destination array entry when the reference does not contain an external calendar ID.
raw_findings.title: Google deletion falls back to primary instead of the configured destination
raw_findings.trigger: A booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, but its event was created in a configured non-primary Google destination calendar.

raw_findings.body: CalendarManager.updateEvent does not populate either `externalId` or `credentialId`, so the recreated references lose both fields. Later reschedules and cancellations cannot reliably select the credential or external calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A successful location edit corrupts the routing metadata stored in BookingReference rows.
raw_findings.impact: CalendarManager.updateEvent does not populate either `externalId` or `credentialId`, so the recreated references lose both fields. Later reschedules and cancellations cannot reliably select the credential or external calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new mapping relies on fields that are only populated by the create path, removing the previous destination-calendar fallback.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Have CalendarManager.updateEvent return the credential ID and supplied external calendar ID, or preserve those values from the existing booking reference when rebuilding references.
raw_findings.title: Location edits replace calendar references with unset routing metadata
raw_findings.trigger: A booking location is edited and `updateLocation` rebuilds references from `updateEvent` results.

raw_findings.body: The new loop updates every `_calendar` reference, including `other_calendar`, and the existing non-traditional integration block updates that same reference again, producing duplicate API calls and potentially duplicate external side effects.
raw_findings.failure_mode: One booking update invokes the same CRM or other-calendar update twice.
raw_findings.impact: The new loop updates every `_calendar` reference, including `other_calendar`, and the existing non-traditional integration block updates that same reference again, producing duplicate API calls and potentially duplicate external side effects.
raw_findings.root_cause: The single-reference path was broadened to all calendar references without accounting for the separate non-traditional-calendar processing block.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Exclude `other_calendar` references from this loop or remove the later dedicated update pass and process each reference exactly once.
raw_findings.title: Non-traditional calendar integrations are updated twice
raw_findings.trigger: A booking has both a traditional calendar reference and a reference whose type contains `other_calendar`, such as a CRM integration.

raw_findings.body: `updateEvent` is called with undefined and throws; the outer catch exits the whole operation, so valid references later in the array are never updated.
raw_findings.failure_mode: One stale host reference prevents every subsequent collective host calendar from being rescheduled.
raw_findings.impact: `updateEvent` is called with undefined and throws; the outer catch exits the whole operation, so valid references later in the array are never updated.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly expanded per-reference loop does not validate the result of its in-memory and database credential lookups before invoking CalendarManager.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the call when credential lookup fails, append a failure result for only that reference, and continue processing the remaining references.
raw_findings.title: A missing referenced credential aborts updates for all remaining hosts
raw_findings.trigger: A multi-host booking contains a reference to a credential that has been deleted or cannot be reconstructed from the database, followed by references to valid host credentials.

raw_findings.body: For each occurrence only the first calendar reference is selected, while the secondary host credential fetched by the outer loop is not used in this branch. Secondary-host events remain active after cancellation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Recurring cancellation removes the primary host event repeatedly and leaves other hosts' calendar events orphaned.
raw_findings.impact: For each occurrence only the first calendar reference is selected, while the secondary host credential fetched by the outer loop is not used in this branch. Secondary-host events remain active after cancellation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The cancellation path was wrapped in a multi-reference outer loop but retained a first-match lookup inside the recurring-booking branch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Iterate all calendar references for every updated booking and resolve each reference's own credential before deleting its event.
raw_findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference
raw_findings.trigger: All remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking with multiple host calendar references are cancelled.

raw_findings.body: CalendarManager receives no `externalId`, so its EventResult and the resulting BookingReference have an undefined externalCalendarId even when the service created the event in a specific non-primary calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: New booking references omit the routing value required for reliable future updates and deletion.
raw_findings.impact: CalendarManager receives no `externalId`, so its EventResult and the resulting BookingReference have an undefined externalCalendarId even when the service created the event in a specific non-primary calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only the credential-ID branch forwards the destination external ID into the newly added EventResult field.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument to `createEvent` in this branch as well.
raw_findings.title: Legacy destination creation drops the external calendar ID from references
raw_findings.trigger: A destination calendar has no credential ID and is handled by the legacy integration-type branch.

raw_findings.body: The organizer object no longer contains its organization slug, so organization-aware booker URLs in event data, emails, or webhooks cannot be constructed correctly.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dynamic organization bookings emit a non-organization or incomplete booker URL.
raw_findings.impact: The organizer object no longer contains its organization slug, so organization-aware booker URLs in event data, emails, or webhooks cannot be constructed correctly.
raw_findings.root_cause: The loadUsers refactor removed a relation that was explicitly selected for downstream organization URL generation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` selection in the dynamic-user query.
raw_findings.title: Dynamic organization users are loaded without organization slug data
raw_findings.trigger: A dynamic booking is made for a user belonging to an organization and the flow later calls `getBookerUrl(organizerUser)`.

raw_findings.body: The payload now supplies an array, including `[]` instead of null, so consumers that access fields such as `destinationCalendar.externalId` break despite this being presented as a non-breaking fix.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Previously compatible webhook integrations fail to parse or use booking events.
raw_findings.impact: The payload now supplies an array, including `[]` instead of null, so consumers that access fields such as `destinationCalendar.externalId` break despite this being presented as a non-breaking fix.
raw_findings.root_cause: An internal CalendarEvent representation change was propagated directly into the public webhook schema.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the existing webhook field shape and add a separate plural field, or version the webhook contract and document a migration path before emitting arrays.
raw_findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar payload is changed without compatibility handling
raw_findings.trigger: An existing webhook consumer receives a booking payload after deployment and expects the documented historical object-or-null destinationCalendar shape.

raw_findings.trigger: An organization is created with either team billing enabled or disabled.
